# Story 81 — Correct a customer's contact details on the customer screen (Story: CRM-68)

---

## Prerequisites

- **CUSTOMERS-7-API (CRM-67)** completed: the `PATCH /api/v1/customers/:id` route exists, accepts a partial `{ name?, email?, phone? }` body, returns the updated customer, and refuses with `{ code, fields: [...] }` on validation / conflict. Contract confirmed against `api/src/features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js` (see acceptance table below).
- Coordinate with the API owner if the shape of the write's response, or the `fields` naming inside a refusal, ever needs to change — the frontend depends on both.

---

## Story Goal

On the customer screen the agent can correct a customer's **name**, **email**, and **phone** in place. The screen sends **only the fields that were edited**, patches the page from the write's answer (no reload), and marks the offending field on a refusal using the shared code sentence. The **Save** control is not offered when nothing changed. Every user-visible string is in both language resource files.

Out of scope: any change under `api/`, deleting a customer, and sending a revision on the write.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the contacts card on the customer screen only **displays** `email` and `phone`; there is no way to correct them from the app.
- **New behaviour:** the same card offers an editable name / email / phone form. Save is only enabled and only rendered when at least one field differs from the loaded value. The write sends **only** the changed fields, patches the screen from the response, and on refusal marks the offending field(s) using the shared `t.errors[code]` sentence.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Add a write hook for the contact correction

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/customers/useCorrectContacts.ts`

Model on `useWriteNote.ts`. Signature:

```ts
import { useCallback } from 'react';

import { request } from '../../shared/api/client';
import { useRequest } from '../../shared/hooks';
import type { Customer } from './useCustomer';

// Only the correctable fields the API accepts. Absent keys are left alone by
// the API; that is what makes the audit diff readable.
export type ContactPatch = Partial<Pick<Customer, 'name' | 'email' | 'phone'>>;

export function useCorrectContacts(customerId: string) {
  const { status, error, run, reset } = useRequest<Customer>();

  const correct = useCallback(
    (patch: ContactPatch) =>
      run(() =>
        request<Customer>(`/customers/${customerId}`, {
          method: 'PATCH',
          body: JSON.stringify(patch),
        }),
      ),
    [run, customerId],
  );

  return { status, error, correct, reset };
}
```

Rules:

- **Do not** send fields the caller did not supply. The hook takes what the screen decides is changed; it never fills in the untouched values.
- One `useRequest` per action — this hook is dedicated to the contacts correction and shares no state with `useWriteNote` or `useGrantSignIn`.
- Import the customer's type from `useCustomer` (the same source `Note` uses on line 24 of `CustomerScreenPage.tsx`). If `useCustomer` does not export `Customer`, add and re-export the type there; do not duplicate the shape.

### 2 — Replace the contacts card on `CustomerScreenPage.tsx` with an editable form

**File:** `web/src/pages/customers/CustomerScreenPage.tsx`

Region to change: the `<Card>` at **lines 86–99** (the `contacts` block that renders `customer.email` / `customer.phone`).

Add near the other hook wiring at **lines 32–41**:

```ts
const correction = useCorrectContacts(id);

const [nameDraft, setNameDraft] = useState('');
const [emailDraft, setEmailDraft] = useState('');
const [phoneDraft, setPhoneDraft] = useState('');
```

Seed and re-seed drafts from the loaded customer whenever the loaded screen changes (mirrors the `useEffect(() => setAdded([]), [screen])` pattern on **line 49**):

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!screen) return;
  setNameDraft(screen.customer.name);
  setEmailDraft(screen.customer.email ?? '');
  setPhoneDraft(screen.customer.phone ?? '');
  correction.reset();
}, [screen]);
```

Compute a diff *only* against the loaded values. **Empty string means "clear the field"** for the nullable ones:

```ts
const patch: ContactPatch = {};
if (screen) {
  if (nameDraft !== screen.customer.name) patch.name = nameDraft;
  const nextEmail = emailDraft.trim() === '' ? null : emailDraft;
  if ((screen.customer.email ?? null) !== nextEmail) patch.email = nextEmail as string;
  const nextPhone = phoneDraft.trim() === '' ? null : phoneDraft;
  if ((screen.customer.phone ?? null) !== nextPhone) patch.phone = nextPhone as string;
}
const changed = Object.keys(patch).length > 0;
```

(The API accepts `null` for a nullable field to clear it — `correct-contacts.test.js` **lines 212–227** confirms `phone: null` is honoured and appears in the audit `after`. Cast is needed because the exported `Customer` type does not carry `null`.)

Submit handler, using the response to patch the screen without reloading:

```ts
const save = async () => {
  if (!changed) return;
  const updated = await correction.correct(patch).catch(() => null);
  if (updated) {
    // The write answers with the customer, the way every other write here does.
    // Patch the in-hand screen instead of reloading the tickets / notes lists.
    reload(); // if useCustomer does not expose a `patchCustomer`, prefer that; otherwise reload.
  }
};
```

**Note on patching without a reload:** the acceptance criterion says "the screen shows the new one without a reload — the write answers with the customer". If `useCustomer` already exposes a way to overwrite only the `customer` slice of `screen` (search for a setter beside `reload`), use it and pass `updated`. Otherwise **add a `patchCustomer(updated)` method to `useCustomer`** that replaces `screen.customer` in place, and use it here. **Do not** call `reload()` — that would refetch tickets and notes for one contact edit and defeats the criterion.

Replace the current contacts card (**lines 86–99**) with an editable form:

```tsx
<Card>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <Text variant="muted">{t.customerScreen.contacts}</Text>

    <Field
      id="customer-name"
      label={t.customerScreen.nameLabel}
      error={fieldError(correction.error, 'name', t)}
    >
      {({ id: fid, describedBy, invalid }) => (
        <Input
          id={fid}
          aria-describedby={describedBy}
          aria-invalid={invalid}
          value={nameDraft}
          onChange={(e) => setNameDraft(e.target.value)}
        />
      )}
    </Field>

    <Field
      id="customer-email"
      label={t.customerScreen.emailLabel}
      error={fieldError(correction.error, 'email', t)}
    >
      {({ id: fid, describedBy, invalid }) => (
        <Input
          id={fid}
          // No native validator (L-55): no type="email", no required.
          // The browser refuses to submit in its own language, outside the
          // resource files, and the API's rule never runs.
          aria-describedby={describedBy}
          aria-invalid={invalid}
          value={emailDraft}
          onChange={(e) => setEmailDraft(e.target.value)}
        />
      )}
    </Field>

    <Field
      id="customer-phone"
      label={t.customerScreen.phoneLabel}
      error={fieldError(correction.error, 'phone', t)}
    >
      {({ id: fid, describedBy, invalid }) => (
        <Input
          id={fid}
          aria-describedby={describedBy}
          aria-invalid={invalid}
          value={phoneDraft}
          onChange={(e) => setPhoneDraft(e.target.value)}
        />
      )}
    </Field>

    {changed ? (
      <Button
        disabled={correction.status === 'loading'}
        onClick={() => void save()}
      >
        {correction.status === 'loading'
          ? t.customerScreen.contactsSaving
          : t.customerScreen.contactsSave}
      </Button>
    ) : null}

    {correction.status === 'error' && correction.error ? (
      <ErrorState
        title={t.customerScreen.contactsFailed}
        body={t.errors[correction.error.code as keyof typeof t.errors] ?? t.errors.INTERNAL}
      />
    ) : null}
  </Stack>
</Card>
```

`fieldError` is a small helper local to the file:

```ts
function fieldError(err: ApiError | null, field: string, t: Translations) {
  if (!err) return undefined;
  if (!Array.isArray(err.fields) || !err.fields.includes(field)) return undefined;
  return t.errors[err.code as keyof typeof t.errors] ?? t.errors.INTERNAL;
}
```

Add `Input` to the destructured import from `'../../shared/ui'` at **lines 4–16** (it is not currently imported there — only `TextArea` is). Add `ApiError` from `'../../shared/api/errors'` for the helper's type.

**Do not** display the raw `<Isolated>` values elsewhere in the card; the `<Input>`s replace them. If the surrounding LTR / RTL comment at **lines 89–91** still matters for read-only values shown elsewhere on the screen, keep it near the relevant markup, not around the form.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **No change made.** `changed === false` → the Save button is not rendered at all. Verified in section 2 above; a test in the plan below asserts the button is absent when drafts equal the loaded values.
- **Only one field edited.** Request body carries exactly one key. The backend contract at `api/src/features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js` **lines 55–86** requires this; the audit `before` / `after` diff key must equal the request key.
- **Clearing the phone.** Draft trimmed to `''` becomes `phone: null` in the patch (nullable per `api/src/features/customers/correct-contacts.test.js` **lines 212–227**). Clearing name is refused server-side with `fields: ['name']` (see **lines 88–98**); the screen marks the name field.
- **Duplicate email (409).** Response `fields: ['email']`, code `CONFLICT`. The email field is marked with `t.errors.CONFLICT`; the form is not cleared; drafts survive.
- **Same-as-existing email (409 on self).** `fields: ['email']` (see **lines 137–147**). Same handling as duplicate.
- **Whole-record validation refusal.** For a corrected field that fails validation the API returns `fields: [<field>]` (see **lines 100–113**); the exact field is marked. When the API returns `fields: ['changes']` for an empty patch, the screen must never fire that request because the Save control is hidden — treat any observed `fields: ['changes']` as a defect in the diff logic.
- **Customer was deleted while the form was open.** `PATCH` returns `404` (see **lines 229–239**). The screen shows the shared `NOT_FOUND` sentence in an `ErrorState`; no field is marked.
- **Concurrent edits on the same screen.** `useRequest` (see `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` **lines 13–18, 46–50**) uses a monotonic ticket so a stale response cannot repaint after a newer save. The seeding `useEffect` in section 2 uses `screen` as its dependency, so a re-seed happens exactly when the loaded customer changes.
- **RTL rendering of the read-only values elsewhere on the screen.** Any remaining places that render `customer.email` / `customer.phone` outside the form must keep the `<Isolated>` wrap (comment at **lines 89–91**).
- **Non-ASCII names.** Accepted; the form is a plain text input, no normalization performed client-side.
- **Native browser validators.** Do **not** add `type="email"` or `required` (L-55): the browser's default message is in the browser's language and outside `t.errors`.

## Done Criteria

- [x] The contact details are editable in place on the customer screen.
- [x] Only the fields somebody edited are sent; a mutation sending all three fails 4 tests.
- [x] The card follows the write's answer — no second read of the customer, and the heading follows too.
- [x] The fields are re-seeded from the answer, so a value the API trimmed is what the field then shows.
- [x] A blank field travels as `null`, the shape the API treats as a value; an empty field that was already empty is not a change.
- [x] Save is not offered when nothing changed, and goes back to disabled when a value is typed back to what it was.
- [x] A field the API named is marked with the shared sentence; a refusal naming none is reported as a failure.
- [x] No native validator on any of the three (L-55), `type="email"` included.
- [x] Both languages (BR-6). `cd web && npm test` (301) and `npm run build` pass; `cd api && npm test` (474) untouched.
- [x] No commit, doc or ignore-file entry mentions AI assistance.

**A regression the failing tests caught, which was not a stale assertion.**
Making the details editable removed the `<bdi>` that `CUSTOMERS-2-WEB` had
added around the email and the phone — and the reason it was added did not go
with it. An input inherits the document's direction, so a phone number on an
Arabic page would be reordered exactly as it was inside an Arabic paragraph:
the groups reverse and the plus lands at the far end. Every field now carries
`dir="auto"`, which is what `<bdi>` does for a value somebody can edit — the
content decides, so a number reads left to right and an Arabic name does not.
A mutation removing it fails.

The two tests that broke were rewritten rather than deleted: one now pins
`dir="auto"` on the fields, the other pins the "no email"/"no phone" words as
placeholders, which is where they went.

**Two things in the plan that were wrong.** It named the error code
`VALIDATION` — it is `VALIDATION_FAILED` — and it listed `CONFLICT` among the
codes this route can return. It cannot: there is no revision on a customer
write, so there is no 409 to handle.

**One thing it suggested that was already there.** `useCustomer` already
exports `Customer`; the "add and re-export the type" task was unnecessary. Its
proposed `patchCustomer` was not built either: `useRequest` holds one answer
and exposes no setter, deliberately, so the page holds the corrected customer
locally — the shape the ticket-categories screen already uses.

Five mutations run: sending the whole form fails 4, omitting a blank instead of
nulling it fails 2, keeping what was typed instead of the answer fails 1,
leaving Save always enabled fails 2, and dropping `dir="auto"` fails 1.
